implementation_statement: No access control policy existed before 2026. POL-02 (P06) was approved 2026-08-31 and becomes effective 2026-09-01; account procedures for the CAD system, PTC workstation, and crew tablets are due 2026-11-30.

Office and TMS accounts are created in the identity provider from HR tickets. CAD accounts are created by the IT Manager in the CAD application with dispatcher, chief dispatcher, and read-only roles. Gaps: accounts of departing employees are disabled 3 to 6 days late; no periodic review; 4 stale contractor administrator accounts on the dispatch servers; 2 dispatch consoles share one Windows login.
evidence: IdP user export; CAD user list; HR termination tickets

implementation_statement: The CAD application enforces role-based access: only dispatcher roles can issue or void track warrants and grant track and time. The TMS enforces clerk, manager, and read-only roles. The PTC back office portal limits locomotive and crew data changes to 2 named administrators.
evidence: CAD role matrix; TMS role export; PTC portal user list

implementation_statement: Not implemented. The office LAN routes to the dispatch VLAN with no filtering, so any office workstation can reach the dispatch servers. Planned: a restricted operations zone with allow-list rules between the office LAN, the dispatch VLAN, and the radio gateway (due 2027-01-31).
evidence: Firewall rule export; P07 SC-7 test

implementation_statement: Dispatchers are standard users on consoles. Gaps: the PTC administration workstation allows email and web browsing under the administrator's session; MSP technicians hold domain administrator rights on the dispatch servers; TSA-marked SSI is readable by all 37 office users.
evidence: Local group export; file share permissions

implementation_statement: Identity provider and domain accounts lock for 15 minutes after 10 failed attempts. The CAD application locks after 5 failures.

Office workstations lock after 15 minutes. Dispatch consoles are exempt so a dispatcher's screen never locks during a live authority; the dispatch center is badge-controlled and staffed 24/7. The PTC administration workstation has no lock (gap).

Two remote paths reach the boundary: the staff remote-access VPN (password only, 23 users) and the dispatch vendor's always-on VPN appliance with one shared vendor account. No session logging on either. Planned: MFA on the staff VPN and vendor access on request only through a jump host (2026-11-30).
The 64 crew tablets are enrolled in device management with encryption, a PIN, and remote wipe. Lost tablets are wiped the same day.
POL-05 (P06) sets training duties. Training procedures for dispatchers and crews are due 2027-02-28.

Office staff complete an annual awareness module. Dispatchers, crews, shop, and maintenance-of-way employees receive none, and no phishing exercises are run. Planned: a short module for all 250 employees, including the rule to report cyber events to dispatch, and quarterly phishing exercises for office staff.
No role-based security training. Planned: dispatcher training on manual dispatch after a cyber outage and on recognizing abnormal CAD behavior; administrator training for the IT staff (2027-02-28).
The CAD application logs log-ons, warrant issuance, and voids. Windows security logging is at default settings on the dispatch servers. The VPN appliance and firewall log to local memory only.
evidence: CAD audit log sample; server audit policy

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: No one reviews logs. Planned: central log workspace in the cloud tenant with weekly review by the IT Manager and alerting through the MSP's managed EDR service (2027-01-31).

CAD application records (warrants and train sheets) are kept for 2 years in the CAD database. Operating system and firewall logs overwrite after about 14 days. Planned: 1-year retention in the log workspace.
evidence: CAD retention setting; server log size

implementation_statement: Logs are generated by the CAD application, servers, identity provider, and cloud tenant, but the VPN appliances and radio gateway generate no retained records.
First control assessment of the TDPO completed 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-07 (P07). Annual assessments are required by POL-01.
No continuous monitoring strategy. Planned: quarterly review of the P01 register, POA&M status, and EDR and scan metrics with the President and General Manager.
The dispatch vendor documents the certified server build. No baseline exists for consoles, the PTC workstation, or network devices.
Office workstations use the MSP's standard settings. Dispatch consoles and the radio gateway use vendor defaults. Default credentials found on 3 wayside detector modems during P07 testing.
evidence: MSP settings report; P07 IA-5 test

implementation_statement: Dispatch consoles run only the CAD client and radio console software. The PTC administration workstation allows email and web browsing (gap).

Office assets are in the MSP's tool. There is no inventory of operations and OT assets (radio gateway, tower equipment, detectors, crossing monitors, PTC workstation, onboard units); the network diagram dates from 2021. Planned: OT asset inventory and a current network diagram (2026-12-31).
POL-01 assigns contingency planning to the Vice President of Operations. No contingency plan procedure yet.

No contingency plan for the TDPO. The manual dispatch procedure (paper track warrants by radio) dates from 2019. Planned: a contingency plan built from the BIA (P05), including manual dispatch, the RSSM location fallback, and the PTC service restoration plan (2026-12-31).
Never tested. Manual dispatch has not been exercised since 2019 and CAD backups have never been restored. Planned: twice-yearly manual dispatch drills and quarterly restore tests.
CAD backups go to a vault in the same cloud account as production workloads. Planned: a separate backup account with immutable retention (2026-12-31).
No alternate dispatch site; the standby CAD server is in the same room as the primary. Planned: standby server and an alternate dispatch desk at the North Yard office (2027-06-30).
Daily backups of both CAD servers to the cloud backup vault, retained 30 days. Not immutable, no offline copy, backup administration shares production credentials.
No documented recovery procedure for the CAD servers or the PTC workstation. Planned with CP-2.
Users are uniquely identified in the identity provider and the CAD application. Gaps: 2 dispatch consoles share one Windows login; the dispatch vendor uses one shared account.
MFA is enforced for identity provider administrators, the cloud console, and the PTC back office portal. Not enforced for server administrator accounts or the VPNs.
MFA is enforced for all users of email, the TMS, and the crew management application through the identity provider. Not enforced on the staff remote-access VPN.

Passwords of 12 or more characters are enforced in the domain and identity provider. Gaps: default manufacturer credentials on 3 wayside detector modems; one shared vendor password not rotated since 2023; the tower shelter padlock key is common to all sites (see PE-3).
POL-03 (P06) approved 2026-08-31. Procedures are the P08 runbook.

No cyber incident handling capability. Physical security events are handled by the Manager of Safety and Security. Planned: P08 ransomware runbook, MSP-managed EDR with 24x7 triage, forensic retainer through the cyber insurer, and a tabletop exercise (2026-11-30).

Physical security concerns are reported to the TSOC within 24 hours. Cyber attacks were not treated as reportable under 49 CFR 1570.203, and a 2025 mailbox compromise was not reported. POL-03 and P08 now list cyber triggers.
regulatory_driver: C-TRANSPORTATION-S01 (1570.203(a)(1); Appendix A to part 1570); C-TRANSPORTATION-S03 (1520.9(c))

implementation_statement: No incident response plan before 2026. POL-03 and the P08 runbook form the plan; approval 2026-08-31, first test due 2026-11-30.

Onboard PTC units are maintained by the mechanical department with the vendor's procedures; failed units are removed and sent for repair (49 CFR 236.1029(a)). Maintenance records for servers and the radio gateway are informal.

The dispatch vendor maintains the CAD servers remotely through an always-on appliance with a shared account and no session logging. The MSP uses its remote management tool on office endpoints. Planned: vendor access on request, through a jump host, with named accounts, MFA, and session recording.

TSA-marked SSI and the hazmat security plan sit in a shared file area open to all office staff. Paper SSI is kept in a locked cabinet in the Safety office. Planned: restricted SSI library with named access (2026-10-31).
Badge access to HQ and the dispatch center is authorized by the Manager of Safety and Security and reviewed each quarter.

Badge readers control HQ and the dispatch center, and the server room is locked. Tower shelters and detector bungalows use one common padlock key held by 22 people; door alarms at the tower sites report to dispatch.
This SSP, approved 2026-08-31.
The IT Manager runs security day to day but is not designated in writing as Cybersecurity Lead (due 2026-09-30).
Background checks at hire for all employees.
HR emails IT at termination and collects tablets and badges. Accounts are disabled 3 to 6 days late. Planned: same-day disable triggered by the HR ticket.
Risk assessment completed 2026-07-24 using SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). Annual update required by POL-01.
No vulnerability scanning. Planned: monthly authenticated scans of office systems and quarterly scans of the dispatch VLAN in maintenance windows agreed with the dispatch vendor.
Contracts with the dispatch vendor, MSP, and AI pilot vendor have no security terms. The PTC back office contract states 99.5% availability but no restoration time or incident notice.

External services in the boundary: PTC back office (SOC 2 Type 2 reviewed 2026 in P09), TMS (SOC 2 Type 2), identity provider, cloud provider. The MSP and the dispatch vendor have never been reviewed.
The CAD version is two releases behind but supported until 2027-12. Dispatch server OS is supported but 2 years behind on patches. Upgrade to be budgeted for 2027.
The HQ firewall blocks inbound traffic except the two VPNs. Internal boundary missing: the office LAN routes freely to the dispatch VLAN. The PTC back office is reached over TLS through the firewall.

implementation_statement: PTC messages use the message integrity and authentication of the host's PTC system (49 CFR 236.1033). The VPNs use IPsec. Detector and crossing monitor alarms travel over public cellular without encryption (gap).
Encryption in the cloud tenant, identity provider, and SaaS services uses provider-managed modules. VPNs use AES-based IPsec suites.
Cloud storage and backups are encrypted at rest by the provider. Dispatch server disks and the PTC workstation are not encrypted.
The MSP patches office endpoints monthly. Dispatch servers are 2 years behind because the vendor certifies patches slowly; radio gateway firmware has not been updated since installation.
evidence: MSP patch report; server build numbers

implementation_statement: MSP-managed signature antivirus on all Windows endpoints and servers. No behavior-based EDR.
No security monitoring. Planned: MSP-managed EDR with 24x7 triage on servers and operations workstations, and alerting from the log workspace (2027-01-31).
No integrity checking of CAD software or backups. Planned: file integrity monitoring on the dispatch servers through EDR, and malware scans of backups before restore.
